caption: Column 1 is λ₁ = 0 and column 2 is λ₂ = π; each eigenvalue alone passes through e^(iλ) while its eigenvector stays put, giving e^(iA) = diag(1, −1). Both new eigenvalues have modulus 1, and that is exactly why the result is unitary.

spec.title: A = diag(0, π) → e^(iA) = diag(1, −1)
spec.aria: Two columns, one per eigenvalue: λ = 0 and λ = π go through e^(iλ) to give 1 and −1, both of modulus 1, so e^(iA) = diag(1, −1).
